featured.title: Nepal Flood Death Toll Surges Past 330 as Glacier Collapse Scale Becomes Clear
featured.excerpt: Scientists confirm an ice-rock avalanche, not an earthquake, triggered one of Nepal's worst natural disasters, with over 900 people still missing including dozens of Americans and 177 Indian pilgrims.
featured.image_caption: An aerial view shows houses buried under mud and debris following flash floods in Nepal on August 26, 2026. The floods killed over 330 people and left more than 900 missing across eight districts.
featured.nri_angle: 177 Indian pilgrims en route to Kailash Mansarovar are among the missing, 63 Americans unaccounted for, and downstream flooding prompted evacuations in Bihar — the disaster has direct implications for diaspora families across South Asia.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

editorial.title: Who Is Anil Chakravarthy? The Bengaluru Boy Who Became a Chancellor's Gold Medalist, an MIT PhD, a Silicon Valley CEO — and Now Adobe's Next Leader
editorial.excerpt: Adobe's board has named Anil Chakravarthy as its next president and CEO, making him the second consecutive Indian-origin leader at the helm of the creative software giant. His journey from Basavanagudi to the C-suite is a story of quiet, methodical ambition.
editorial.image_caption: Anil Chakravarthy, who has been named Adobe's next CEO effective December 1, 2026, succeeding Shantanu Narayen.
editorial.nri_angle: Adobe's CEO succession from one Indian-origin leader to another underscores the growing dominance of Indian-educated executives in global tech leadership.
editorial.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Baba Ramdev's 'Ayurvedic Hookah' Ignites Memes, Mockery and a Medical Warning

just_in.excerpt: The 'pay on delivery fee' appears as a separate line in the bill summary on cash orders, on top of platform fees, packaging charges and GST — while online payments remain exempt.

just_in.nri_angle: Bollywood's role as India's soft-power export resonates strongly with the diaspora, who recognize these songs as shared cultural touchstones wherever they live.

just_in.title: Ralph Lauren Faces Backlash for Uncredited Zardozi Gown at Fashion Week
just_in.excerpt: A Spring 2027 gown shown in New York was described by the brand as having "hand-applied embellishments" — with no mention of India or zardozi. Critics say this is how global fashion erases the artisans behind the work.

just_in.excerpt: A Bengaluru court's interim order pits two funded startups — AppsForBharat's Sri Mandir and Way2News's Veda Mandir — against each other over confidential data allegedly carried out the door by a former employee. Way2News denies everything.

just_in.title: Anthropic's Amodei Proposes Three-Step Plan to Slow the Pace of AI
just_in.excerpt: In a new essay, Anthropic's CEO argues AI capabilities are outpacing the industry's ability to control them — and lays out a three-pronged framework that has already won agreement from Sam Altman and Elon Musk.

just_in.nri_angle: Indian-origin AI researchers and engineers at frontier labs are central to this debate; pacing rules would directly shape how they build and evaluate models.

just_in.title: Nifty Clings to Support as Fed Decision and $104 Crude Set the Week's Direction
just_in.excerpt: After five straight weekly losses, the index holds near the 23,000–23,300 support band with the Fed's September 16 call and elevated oil prices set to decide what comes next.

just_in.title: RBI Rejection Leaves Tata Sons Running Out of Room to Avoid a Listing
just_in.excerpt: The central bank's September 11 letter rejects Tata Sons' bid to surrender its NBFC registration, keeping the upper-layer listing mandate intact as leadership churn compounds the pressure.

just_in.nri_angle: A Tata Sons IPO would be one of India's largest ever, giving NRI investors direct exposure to the holding company behind TCS, Tata Motors and Air India — and forcing long-overdue disclosure of capital flows through the group.

news.title: Stalked for Months, Reported Again and Again: Indian-Origin Woman Shot Dead in Sacramento
news.excerpt: Shalini Thakur, 38, had told Sacramento deputies about a tracker hidden in her car and secured a restraining order months before she was killed. The suspect was later found dead after a freeway standoff.
news.nri_angle: An Indian-origin woman was killed in California after months of documented stalking, raising diaspora concerns about victim safety, and the suspect's immigration history has made the case a U.S. enforcement debate flashpoint.

news.title: India and China Can Build a Multipolar World, Says Economist Jeffrey Sachs
news.excerpt: The Columbia economist told India Today that within 25 years, India and China will be the world's two largest economies, and that closer cooperation between them could anchor a genuinely multilateral order.
news.image_caption: The flags of India and China with an inset photo of economist Jeffrey Sachs. Sachs told India Today that India will become the world largest economy at some point this century.
news.nri_angle: Sachs' forecast reinforces the long-term growth case for India that many NRIs are already investing behind, while his critique of US tariffs speaks to diaspora concerns about the bilateral relationship.

news.title: Modi Meets Tokayev, El-Sisi as Xi and Putin Depart After BRICS Summit
news.excerpt: On the final day of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the prime minister held bilateral talks with Kazakhstan's Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Egypt's Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, as the summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration and Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin departed.

news.title: Amit Shah Sets 2029 Deadline for Uniform Civil Code in 21 NDA-Ruled States
news.excerpt: Speaking in Mumbai, the Union home minister said BJP-led NDA governments in 21 states would introduce a common civil code before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections, and announced a month-long campaign marking Narendra Modi's 25 years in public life.
news.image_caption: Union Home Minister Amit Shah. He said all 21 NDA-ruled states will implement the Uniform Civil Code before the 2029 general elections.
news.nri_angle: For NRIs with property and family ties in India, a common code governing inheritance and succession across states could simplify estate matters, though the rollout is several years out.

news.title: Indian-Origin Surrey Landlady Arrested After Tenant's Viral Harassment Videos
news.excerpt: Raj Tiwana was taken into custody by Surrey Police after a tenant documented alleged harassment, unauthorized entries, and physical confrontations in videos that spread widely online. Police have issued no official statement, and the exact charges remain unclear.

news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Indian-Origin Woman Charged With Two First-Degree Murders in California Killings
news.excerpt: Anila Baby, 32, allegedly killed two friends from Kerala in separate attacks about 90 minutes apart on August 28, and faces 50 years to life in prison if convicted.
news.image_caption: Anila Baby in a booking photo. The 32-year-old is charged with two counts of first-degree murder in the killings of two friends in San Jose and Milpitas, California.

news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Russian drones kill 2 at Ukraine-Moldova border crossing; Zelenskyy demands global action

nri-world.title: Virat Kohli Meets Maharashtra Deputy CM Eknath Shinde in London
nri-world.excerpt: The goodwill meeting during Shinde's UK visit covered sports, infrastructure, and state welfare schemes; the Deputy CM felicitated Kohli with a shawl and bouquet.
nri-world.image_caption: Virat Kohli. The India star met Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde during his visit to London.
nri-world.nri_angle: Kohli, who lives in London, and Shinde's diaspora-facing announcements underscore the UK Indian community's role as a bridge between Indian politics and its global audience.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: "Talent Is Universal, Opportunity Is Not": Wadhwani Foundation CEO Dr. Ajay Kela on Why the Diaspora's Greatest Asset Isn't Money
nri-world.excerpt: In an exclusive interview with The Videshi, the CEO of Wadhwani Foundation talks about India's innovation ecosystem, the "missing middle" of Indian entrepreneurship, and why the diaspora's most powerful currency isn't capital — it's knowledge.
nri-world.image_caption: Dr. Ajay Kela, CEO and Board Member of Wadhwani Foundation, leads the organization's mission to create 5 million jobs and upskill 25 million people across emerging economies.
nri-world.nri_angle: Interview with Dr. Ajay Kela, NRI leader who returned to India to lead Wadhwani Foundation — covers diaspora giving back, deep-tech opportunities, and India's innovation ecosystem.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Justice Department Sues Arkansas Over In-State Tuition for Immigrant Students
immigration.excerpt: Thursday's lawsuits against Arkansas, Hawaii, Utah and D.C. bring the administration's total to 25, as the DOJ says it has now challenged every state offering tuition breaks to noncitizens.
immigration.image_caption: The Arkansas State Capitol in Little Rock. The Justice Department has sued Arkansas, Hawaii, Utah and Washington, D.C., over laws granting in-state tuition to noncitizen students.
immigration.nri_angle: The outcome matters well beyond Arkansas: immigrant families across the 25 sued states — including Indian students and work-authorized families paying in-state rates — face the prospect of sharply higher college costs.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Immigration Court Waits Keep Rising Even as Deportations Hit Record Pace
immigration.excerpt: TRAC data show people ordered removed in July waited an average of 901 days — up 51% in two years — even as judges completed a record 104,028 deportation cases.
immigration.image_caption: The Bishop Henry Whipple Federal Building near Minneapolis, which houses an immigration court. The court backlog has passed 3 million cases, with backlogged cases waiting an average of 940 days, according to TRAC.
immigration.nri_angle: For immigrants of all nationalities navigating the U.S. system, the data point to longer years of legal limbo even as the machinery of removal runs faster than ever.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: ACLU Sues Hartford Immigration Court Over Withheld Basic Case Records
immigration.excerpt: The Connecticut ACLU chapter filed a federal lawsuit this week against the U.S. attorney general and Hartford's chief immigration judge, arguing the public has a First Amendment right to docket numbers, case captions, and in absentia removal orders without waiting months for a FOIA response.
immigration.image_caption: The Abraham A. Ribicoff Federal Building in Hartford, Connecticut, which houses the Hartford immigration court. The ACLU has sued the court over withheld basic case records.
immigration.nri_angle: Indian immigrants navigating asylum or removal proceedings in Connecticut depend on public scrutiny of immigration courts to ensure their cases receive fair process.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: El Salvador TPS Holds Past Its Deadline as Employers Await DHS Guidance
immigration.excerpt: The designation's September 9 expiry passed with no Federal Register notice from DHS, leaving beneficiaries protected but employers without updated I-9 instructions.
immigration.image_caption: The national flag of El Salvador. DHS has not issued a termination or extension notice for the TPS designation, leaving employers without updated Form I-9 guidance.
immigration.nri_angle: Immigration-watch readers — including employers of TPS workers and diaspora members tracking DHS policy shifts — need to know what remains in effect and where the documentation gap lies.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Indian man jailed 27 years in Australia for fatal stabbing, faces deportation
immigration.excerpt: Robin Robin, 30, was sentenced in the Victorian Supreme Court for murdering 22-year-old Navjeet Singh Sandhu and attempting to murder Sharwan Singh during a drunken rampage in Ormond in May 2024. He will not be eligible for parole for 20 years and is expected to be deported to India.
immigration.image_caption: Melbourne, where the Victorian Supreme Court sentenced Robin Robin to 27 years in prison for a fatal stabbing in Ormond.
immigration.nri_angle: The sentencing shows how a serious criminal conviction in Australia leads to visa cancellation and post-sentence deportation for Indian nationals, a direct warning for the large Indian student and migrant community.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: DHS Proposes $103,265 Fee on Every H-1B Cap Petition in Sweeping Rulemaking
immigration.excerpt: DHS says the fee would recover $8.8 billion a year in federal immigration costs. Unlike the struck-down $100,000 order, it would apply even to F-1 students changing status inside the U.S.
immigration.image_caption: The U.S. Capitol in Washington. The Department of Homeland Security has proposed a $103,265 fee on every H-1B cap petition.
immigration.nri_angle: Indian nationals receive the largest share of H-1B visas, so a six-figure fee would sharply raise employer costs for hiring Indian tech workers and could cool H-1B demand.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: September Visa Bulletin Brings Biggest Family Green Card Advances in Years
immigration.excerpt: Family-sponsored final action dates jumped by up to 29 months, with India gaining in F2B and F3 — but employment-based categories froze and India EB-2 stays unavailable.
immigration.image_caption: Immigration paperwork, including an Affidavit of Support form, an IRS account transcript, and a calculator on a desk. The State Department's September 2026 Visa Bulletin brought some of the largest forward movements in recent years across family-sponsored green card categories.
immigration.nri_angle: Indian family-sponsored applicants gain years of forward movement in F2B and F3, while Indian professionals in employment-based lines see no relief and face possible retrogression before October.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: DOL Suspends New PERM Green Card Filings by Cognizant, Cloudera
immigration.excerpt: The Labor Department's inspector general froze new permanent labor certification filings at the two tech firms amid a fraud probe — stalling green card sponsorships for thousands of H-1B workers, with no charges yet announced.
immigration.image_caption: TR Immigration social card image accompanying its report on the PERM filing suspensions. The Labor Department inspector general announced on September 8, 2026 that new permanent labor certification filings by Cognizant and Cloudera were frozen during a fraud investigation.
immigration.nri_angle: The freeze stalls green card sponsorships for thousands of Indian H-1B professionals at Cognizant and Cloudera, including the six-year extensions that depend on pending PERM or approved I-140 petitions.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: ESDS Soars 92% in First Full Week as New-Age Tech Stocks End Mixed
markets-finance.excerpt: Cloud infrastructure firm ESDS quadrupled its IPO price in a week of upper circuits, while fintechs rallied on hopes of a UPI merchant discount rate during Global Fintech Fest 2026.
markets-finance.image_caption: An Inc42 graphic for its weekly new-age tech stocks coverage shows bull and bear figures alongside Pine Labs and ESDS branding. ESDS led the week's gainers with a 91.65% surge in its first full week of trading.
markets-finance.nri_angle: The MDR debate directly affects the economics of India's digital payments stack that many diaspora investors track through fintech holdings like Paytm and Pine Labs.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Nifty Clings to Support as Fed Decision and $104 Crude Set the Week's Direction
markets-finance.excerpt: After five straight weekly losses, the index holds near the 23,000–23,300 support band with the Fed's September 16 call and elevated oil prices set to decide what comes next.
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRI portfolios with Indian equity exposure, the confluence of a potential Fed hike, $104 crude and a weakening rupee argues for defensive positioning — healthcare and pharma — until the week's macro catalysts clear.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: RBI Rejection Leaves Tata Sons Running Out of Room to Avoid a Listing
markets-finance.excerpt: The central bank's September 11 letter rejects Tata Sons' bid to surrender its NBFC registration, keeping the upper-layer listing mandate intact as leadership churn compounds the pressure.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Tata logo displayed on a corporate sign. The Reserve Bank of India has rejected Tata Sons bid to surrender its NBFC registration, keeping its mandatory listing requirement alive.
markets-finance.nri_angle: A Tata Sons IPO would be one of India's largest ever, giving NRI investors direct exposure to the holding company behind TCS, Tata Motors and Air India — and forcing long-overdue disclosure of capital flows through the group.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: NSE Leads Rs 24,600 Crore IPO Bonanza With 11 Issues Opening Next Week
markets-finance.excerpt: Eleven IPOs targeting a combined Rs 24,574 crore open for subscription next week, headlined by the NSE's long-awaited Rs 22,569 crore listing — India's second-largest public issue ever — alongside a Rs 1,000 crore Hero Motors offering.
markets-finance.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange building in Mumbai. The NSE's Rs 22,569 crore IPO opens September 17, India's second-largest ever after Hyundai Motor India's 2024 listing.
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI and OCI investors can participate in Indian IPOs through NRE/NRO accounts under FEMA rules, so the year's headline offerings — including the NSE listing — are directly accessible to the diaspora.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Overtakes Russia as Fourth-Largest Forex Reserve Holder After Record $44.9B Surge
markets-finance.excerpt: The RBI said reserves jumped a record $44.9 billion to a lifetime high of $785.7 billion in the week ended September 4, driven by the central bank's FCNR(B) deposit scheme — with a Rs 1 lakh crore bond sale now planned to mop up excess liquidity.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building in Mumbai. Forex reserves rose a record $44.9 billion to $785.7 billion, lifting India past Russia to become the world's fourth-largest holder.
markets-finance.nri_angle: A record forex stockpile strengthens the rupee's floor against global shocks, which directly affects exchange rates for remittances and the returns of India-linked portfolios.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Global Funds Lose Faith in India as Some Cut Stock Allocations to Zero
markets-finance.excerpt: Money managers at Janus Henderson and Vantage Point have pared India exposure to zero, and foreign portfolio ownership has tumbled to a 17-year low as AI-rich North Asia steals the flows.
markets-finance.image_caption: An illustration shows hands pulling apart the pieces of a red pie chart. Global funds have pulled a net $25 billion from Indian stocks this year, with foreign portfolio ownership of NSE-listed companies falling to a 17-year low.
markets-finance.nri_angle: India raised $127 billion from its diaspora to defend the rupee, showing how directly overseas Indians are being pulled into the country's currency battle — and NRI portfolios tied to Indian equities are feeling the foreign exodus first-hand.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: TSMC Posts Record August Revenue as AI Boom Keeps Foundries Fully Booked
markets-finance.excerpt: Taiwan Semiconductor posted NT$514.8 billion in August sales — up 53% from a year ago — but investors barely blinked, with the stock slipping as the AI trade shows signs of fatigue.
markets-finance.image_caption: TSMC chairman C.C. Wei. TSMC posted record August revenue of NT$514.8 billion, up 53.3% from a year earlier, as AI chip demand kept its advanced foundries fully booked.
markets-finance.nri_angle: TSMC anchors most semiconductor and emerging-market index funds held by global investors, so its guidance and pricing power shape portfolios well beyond Taiwan.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: US Consumer Sentiment Plunges in September as Inflation Fears Mount
markets-finance.excerpt: The University of Michigan's sentiment index fell to 47.8 in early September while year-ahead inflation expectations jumped to 4.6%, the highest since June.
markets-finance.image_caption: Shoppers at a supermarket. The University of Michigan's Consumer Sentiment Index fell to 47.8 in early September as inflation expectations jumped.
markets-finance.nri_angle: With sentiment near historic lows and inflation expectations rising, diaspora households should factor weaker hiring prospects and persistent grocery and fuel costs into fall spending and home-buying decisions.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Gavaskar Slams Domestic Format: 'How Does a Team Learn to Take 20 Wickets?'
sports.excerpt: In his Mid-Day column, the batting legend cited the Duleep Trophy final — where East Zone batted on and shook hands instead of pushing for an outright win — to explain India's Test struggles.
sports.image_caption: Sunil Gavaskar. The former India captain questioned how teams can learn to take 20 wickets under the current domestic format.
sports.nri_angle: Diaspora fans who watch India struggle to finish sides on flat pitches will recognize Gavaskar's diagnosis: domestic cricket rewards batting longer, not bowling better, and the Test side inherits the habit.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: KL Rahul in Line for ODI Vice-Captaincy as Asian Games Clash Hits India's Plans
sports.excerpt: With Shreyas Iyer leading India at the Asian Games in Japan, the vice-captaincy under Shubman Gill is open for the September 27 ODI series — and the second wicketkeeper slot has become a Pant vs Jurel debate.
sports.image_caption: KL Rahul trains with the Indian cricket team wearing the blue India kit and helmet. He is the front-runner to be named India vice-captain for the three-match ODI series against the West Indies.
sports.nri_angle: A home ODI series with Kohli back and a new-look India is primetime diaspora viewing, and the Asian Games overlap means fans get two Indian teams playing on different continents in the same week.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Tanvi Patri, 15, Wins U17 Crown in All-Indian Final at Asia Junior Championships
sports.excerpt: The 15-year-old from Odisha beat compatriot Shaina Manimuthu 11-15, 15-10, 15-12 in Chengdu, capping a breakthrough 2026 season that already includes her first international title.
sports.nri_angle: Another Indian teenager winning Asian age-group titles against Chinese and Japanese competition strengthens the junior pipeline diaspora fans are watching as the senior women's singles ranks need fresh faces.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Nepal Beat UAE to Win ACC Premier Cup and Book Asia Cup 2027 Spot
sports.excerpt: Aasif Sheikh's century and Gulsan Jha's late assault powered Nepal to 313, before Karan KC and Lalit Rajbanshi derailed a UAE chase anchored by Rahul Chopra's unbeaten hundred at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur.
sports.image_caption: Nepal's players celebrate with the trophy and a champions banner after winning the ACC Men's Premier Cup 2026 final. Nepal beat the UAE by 44 runs in Kuala Lumpur to seal qualification for the Asia Cup 2027.
sports.nri_angle: The UAE's squad is stacked with Indian-origin players, including captain Harpreet Singh Bhatia and centurion Rahul Chopra, highlighting the diaspora's role in Gulf cricket.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Harleen Deol Joins Barbados Tridents for Remainder of WCPL 2026
sports.excerpt: The 28-year-old India batter becomes the fifth Indian in this year's Women's Caribbean Premier League, linking up with Kiran Navgire and Pooja Vastrakar for her first global franchise stint.
sports.image_caption: Harleen Deol celebrates with the Indian flag after India’s ODI World Cup triumph in 2025. The 28-year-old batter has signed with the Barbados Tridents for the remainder of the WCPL 2026 season.
sports.nri_angle: A fifth Indian joins the Caribbean league, with three Indians now in the defending champions' squad.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Rajeev Ram Retires After US Open Semifinal Loss, Ending Storied Doubles Career
sports.excerpt: The former world No. 1 doubles star played his final match alongside Joe Salisbury on September 11, then gave a tearful on-court farewell honoring his late father.
sports.image_caption: Rajeev Ram receives a commemorative frame during his on-court farewell ceremony at the US Open. The former doubles world No. 1 retired after playing his final match on September 11, 2026.
sports.nri_angle: The greatest Indian-American tennis player of all time says goodbye at the tournament where he built his legacy.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Afghanistan vs India T20Is: Full Schedule, Squads and How to Watch
sports.excerpt: Three T20 internationals at Delhi's Arun Jaitley Stadium on September 13, 15 and 17 — Afghanistan's first series as host against India, with Jasprit Bumrah back in India's squad.
sports.image_caption: India players gather in a huddle during a T20I match, wearing the team blue kit sponsored by Apollo Tyres. India face Afghanistan in a three-match T20I series at Delhis Arun Jaitley Stadium on September 13, 15 and 17, 2026.
sports.nri_angle: The series sits at the intersection of two of cricket's most followed fan bases — the Indian and Afghan diasporas in the UK, North America and the Gulf — with morning start times in North America making the games easy to follow live.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Babar Azam Enters Record Books With 2,000 WTC Runs as Captain
sports.excerpt: The Pakistan captain's 76 at Edgbaston made him the fourth batter — and second Asian — to reach 2,000 World Test Championship runs as captain, a milestone that eluded India's Kohli and Rohit. But England completed a 3-0 whitewash.
sports.image_caption: Babar Azam. The former Pakistan captain became only the fourth captain to score 2,000 runs in the World Test Championship, reaching the milestone at Edgbaston.
sports.nri_angle: A record that eluded Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma as captains gives subcontinent cricket fans — including millions in the diaspora — a fresh statistical lens on Babar Azam's standing, even as Pakistan's tour ended in a 3-0 whitewash.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Bumrah Finds Rhythm in Delhi Nets Ahead of Afghanistan T20I Return
sports.excerpt: Bowling at full intensity in Thursday's Delhi nets, Jasprit Bumrah looked ready for his first T20I since March. Shreyas Iyer wants him to get game time; Afghanistan say they have a plan for him.
sports.image_caption: Jasprit Bumrah. The pacer bowled at full intensity in the Delhi nets on Thursday as he closes in on a T20I return against Afghanistan.
sports.nri_angle: Bumrah's injury comeback is the biggest storyline in Indian cricket for diaspora fans, and the Afghanistan series — played entirely in Delhi — offers a rare home-format tune-up before the Asian Games.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Divyanshi Choudhary Breaks Down After Last-Minute Asian Games Wushu Axing
sports.excerpt: The 18-year-old wushu player beat Roshibina Devi in the selection trials and had already collected her India kit for Aichi-Nagoya — then was dropped days before departure, citing a knee injury her camp calls treatable.
sports.image_caption: Sanda competition. Divyanshi Choudhary, 18, was dropped from India's Asian Games 2026 squad in the women's 60kg Sanda category days before departure.
sports.nri_angle: Selection transparency and athlete welfare in Indian sports — a governance issue diaspora fans follow closely as India chases medals beyond cricket at the Asian Games.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Anmol Ekka Double Fires India Into Fourth Straight Junior Asia Cup Final
sports.excerpt: India beat Malaysia 3-1 in Moqi, China, with captain Ekka scoring twice and goalkeeper Vivek Lakra saving a penalty stroke; South Korea await in Sunday's final.
sports.image_caption: India's junior men's hockey team in action. Anmol Ekka's double fired the defending champions into a fourth straight Junior Asia Cup final.
sports.nri_angle: Anmol Ekka's 16-goal breakout gives diaspora hockey fans a new star to follow as India's junior pipeline builds toward the Junior World Cup.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's New Zealand Tour Sells 50,000 Tickets in Two Weeks
sports.excerpt: NZ Cricket sold more than 50,000 tickets in just over two weeks for India's first tour in six years, reopening Eden Park's sixth tier for the first time since 2019.
sports.image_caption: A packed cricket stadium under lights during a night match. Tickets for India's tour of New Zealand sold 50,000 seats within two weeks.
sports.nri_angle: India fixtures draw the largest and loudest diaspora crowds of any touring side in New Zealand, home to one of the world's fastest-growing Indian communities.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's Chip Sector Hits $1.4 Billion in Funding as Dholera Fab Races Toward 2027
technology.excerpt: A Tracxn report timed to SEMICON India 2026 shows funding up 10x since 2021 — but services and design still dominate, and no approved fab is in commercial production yet.
technology.image_caption: A semiconductor chip mounted on a printed circuit board. A new Tracxn report says India's chip sector has drawn $1.4 billion in cumulative equity funding across 281 companies.
technology.nri_angle: India's semiconductor buildout matters to diaspora investors and the thousands of Indian-origin chip engineers in the US who may follow the fabs home; US-China tech decoupling makes India's foundry bet a global supply-chain story.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Bengaluru Court Bars Way2News From Using AppsForBharat's Confidential Data
technology.excerpt: A Bengaluru court's interim order pits two funded startups — AppsForBharat's Sri Mandir and Way2News's Veda Mandir — against each other over confidential data allegedly carried out the door by a former employee. Way2News denies everything.
technology.image_caption: An Inc42 graphic shows AppsForBharat's branding and its Sri Mandir app against a temple backdrop. The startup won an interim court order restraining Way2News from using its confidential data.
technology.nri_angle: The Sri Mandir app serves millions of devotees including diaspora users who book remote pujas; the legal fight over who controls that platform's data and content matters to the community that relies on it.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Anthropic's Amodei Proposes Three-Step Plan to Slow the Pace of AI
technology.excerpt: In a new essay, Anthropic's CEO argues AI capabilities are outpacing the industry's ability to control them — and lays out a three-pronged framework that has already won agreement from Sam Altman and Elon Musk.
technology.image_caption: An editorial illustration shows a person working at a computer beneath a padlock and Anthropic branding. It accompanied coverage of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's call to slow the pace of frontier AI development.
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin AI researchers and engineers at frontier labs are central to this debate; pacing rules would directly shape how they build and evaluate models.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: MIT's Injectable 'Nanoantennas' Destroy Drug-Resistant Brain Cancer Cells
technology.excerpt: The magnetically activated HITMAN technology eliminated 52 percent of chemotherapy-resistant glioblastoma cells in lab tests and extended survival in mice, without harming healthy brain tissue.
technology.image_caption: An illustration of injectable nanoantennas being wirelessly activated by a magnetic field to target a brain tumor. MIT Media Lab researchers developed the HITMAN technology to destroy drug-resistant glioblastoma cells while leaving healthy tissue unharmed.
technology.nri_angle: The breakthrough was led by MIT Media Lab's Deblina Sarkar, an Indian-origin researcher heading the Nano-Cybernetic Biotrek group.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: After Anthropic Researcher's Extinction Warning, Congress Demands AI Safeguards
technology.excerpt: More than 20 members of Congress called for federal AI regulation this week after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon's viral resignation warning, with Rep. Lori Trahan declaring bipartisan momentum has hit “a tipping point.”
technology.image_caption: The U.S. Capitol in Washington. More than 20 members of Congress have called for stronger AI regulation after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon quit, warning the industry is ‘gambling with our lives.’
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers make up a significant share of the U.S. AI workforce, so any federal regime of testing mandates, development pauses, or a new AI safety agency would land directly on the labs that employ them.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Trezor Brevo Breach Exposed 347,000 Emails to Phishing Attack
technology.excerpt: A flaw in email provider Brevo's login system let attackers send phishing emails from Trezor's own domain to 347,000 newsletter subscribers — the hardware wallet maker's second third-party data breach in weeks.
technology.nri_angle: Crypto ownership runs deep in the Indian diaspora, so wallet-holding readers should scrutinize vendor-branded emails and warn family members about the phishing campaign.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: The AI 'Doomsday' Debate Moves From Silicon Valley to Mainstream America
technology.excerpt: A departing Anthropic researcher's warning about civilization-ending AI has triggered the week's biggest tech story — and new calls in Congress for guardrails.
technology.image_caption: A data center housing AI infrastructure. The debate over catastrophic AI risk has moved from Silicon Valley circles into mainstream American discourse.
technology.nri_angle: Indian engineers form a large share of the AI research workforce, so both a regulatory crackdown and unchecked deployment would land directly on diaspora careers.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: TCS Opens India's First Lights-Out Factory Lab in Pune for AI Manufacturing
technology.excerpt: The Industrial Autonomy & Engineering Lab features a fully robotic battery pack assembly line where manufacturers can prototype AI-first production systems before deploying them in real factories.
technology.image_caption: A robotic arm works on an automated factory production line. TCS launched its Industrial Autonomy & Engineering Lab, described as India's first lights-out factory lab for AI-led manufacturing, at its Pune campus on September 9.
technology.nri_angle: The lab advances India's positioning in AI-led manufacturing, a sector diaspora investors and tech professionals watch as a signal of where global industrial AI work is heading.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Jio Payment Solutions Launches Cross-Border Platform for Indian Exporters
technology.excerpt: The Jio Financial Services unit won RBI authorization to operate as a cross-border payment aggregator, offering multi-currency virtual accounts that let exporters skip SWIFT and correspondent banking.
technology.image_caption: The Jio logo. Jio Payment Solutions has launched a cross-border payments platform aimed at Indian exporters.
technology.nri_angle: Diaspora entrepreneurs and freelance professionals doing business with India gain a regulated, lower-friction rail for getting paid across borders.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Anthropic Researcher Quits, Says AI Labs Are 'Gambling With Our Lives'
technology.excerpt: Jacob Coxon, who did pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic, resigned warning that frontier labs are racing to self-improving superintelligence — and was publicly backed by Anthropic's own alignment science lead.
technology.image_caption: A robotic hand hovers over a keyboard in front of a blurred Anthropic logo in a Reuters illustration. AI researcher Jacob Coxon resigned from Anthropic on September 9, 2026, warning that frontier labs were "gambling with our lives" in the race to superintelligence.
technology.nri_angle: Indian engineers and researchers inside frontier AI labs are central to the technology — and the safety debate Coxon ignited affects the industry many diaspora professionals work in.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: 'Main Na Raha Mera' First Look: Adhyayan Suman's Musical Romance Sets Teaser for September 16
entertainment.excerpt: Adhyayan Suman's romantic musical pairs him with former Miss Universe India Divita Rai in a 90s-nostalgia love story built around ego versus love.
entertainment.image_caption: A still from the announcement motion poster of 'Main Na Raha Mera', showing an open journal inside a tent at dusk. The film stars Adhyayan Suman opposite Divita Rai, with the first look released by T-Series.
entertainment.nri_angle: Nostalgia for 1990s Bollywood romance resonates strongly with the diaspora, and the beauty-queen-to-Bollywood pipeline is a well-tracked phenomenon for NRI entertainment readers.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Bollywood Takes Over BRICS: Anwar Ibrahim and an Indonesian Journalist Sing Hindi Classics in Delhi
entertainment.excerpt: The Malaysian prime minister sang a Kishore Kumar classic at a BRICS gala dinner while an Indonesian journalist performed a 1990s hit — as serious diplomacy, including an upgraded India-Malaysia partnership, moved forward offstage.
entertainment.image_caption: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim sings at a piano during a BRICS gala dinner in New Delhi. He performed Kishore Kumar's 1965 classic "Khwab Ho Tum Ya Koi Haqeeqat" from the film Teen Devian.
entertainment.nri_angle: Bollywood's role as India's soft-power export resonates strongly with the diaspora, who recognize these songs as shared cultural touchstones wherever they live.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Ralph Lauren Faces Backlash for Uncredited Zardozi Gown at Fashion Week
entertainment.excerpt: A Spring 2027 gown shown in New York was described by the brand as having "hand-applied embellishments" — with no mention of India or zardozi. Critics say this is how global fashion erases the artisans behind the work.

entertainment.nri_angle: The diaspora sits at the center of this debate — Indian-American designers and consumers have been among the loudest voices demanding global brands name the crafts they borrow.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Diljit Dosanjh Makes History as First Punjabi Singer to Headline Wembley

entertainment.title: Mirzapur The Movie Crosses $2 Million In North America, Climbing Indian Box Office Charts

lifestyle-health.title: Baba Ramdev's 'Ayurvedic Hookah' Ignites Memes, Mockery and a Medical Warning
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A viral video shows the yoga guru loading a hookah with herbs and claiming it balances the doshas. Doctors say inhaling any smoke is no therapy.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Yoga guru Baba Ramdev in a still from the viral Instagram video showing his so-called ayurvedic hookah. Medical experts say inhaling any smoke is not a safe therapy for cough or congestion, despite the herbal ingredients.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Ramdev's Patanjali products have a large diaspora following; diaspora families navigating Ayurveda-meets-wellness-trend claims need clear medical context on what's tradition and what's marketing.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Could Your Daily Coffee Habit Actually Slow Down Aging?
lifestyle-health.excerpt: From protective brain receptors to large-scale mortality studies, researchers find moderate coffee drinking is linked with healthier aging — but the evidence comes with important caveats.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A cup of coffee. Large observational studies link two to three cups a day with lower risks of early death, though researchers stress the findings show association, not causation.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: India's diaspora is swapping filter kaapi for espresso culture — the research's two-to-three-cup sweet spot, with decaf as a viable option, fits both traditions.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Ozempic and Wegovy May Carry a Hair-Loss Risk for Some Men
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new NYU Langone study finds the first genetic link between GLP-1 drugs and male-pattern hair loss — but researchers stress the evidence is early and applies only to men already genetically predisposed.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Ozempic injection pens. An NYU Langone Health study found men genetically predisposed to pattern baldness face roughly 7 percent higher odds of hair loss with GLP-1 drugs.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: GLP-1 medications are widely used by Indian-American patients managing diabetes and obesity; those noticing unusual shedding should raise it with their doctor rather than abandoning a treatment whose metabolic benefits are well established.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Third of Americans May Have Fatty Liver Disease — Diet Is the Fix
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Up to 42% of American adults may have fat building up in their livers without knowing it. Doctors say the fix isn't a cleanse — it's what you eat every day.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. Between 30 and 40 percent of American adults have excess fat stored in their livers, and gastroenterologists say diet is the first-line treatment.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For Indian-American households, where rich festive foods and sedentary workdays are common — and where metabolic disease strikes at lower body weights — the hepatologists' dietary advice is directly relevant family-health guidance.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Fat Cells Keep Hunger Signal Stuck 'On' After Weight Loss, Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Case Western Reserve researchers say a lasting "obesity memory" in fat tissue may explain why weight returns after dieting or stopping GLP-1 drugs — and can pass from mother to child.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: The study’s graphical abstract shows how fat cells retain an "obesity memory" that keeps appetite high after weight loss, and how the signal passes from mother to child. The research was published in Cell Reports by scientists at Case Western Reserve University and the Harrington Discovery Institute.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: India's growing obesity and diabetes burden makes the weight-regain problem familiar to diaspora families; the study was led by Indian-origin scientist Dr. Atul Chopra.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Cardiologist Urges Earlier ECG Screening for At-Risk Patients as India's Heart Disease Burden Grows
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Dr. Vijay D'Silva says skipping early ECG screening costs lives — but U.S. guidelines add an important caveat: screening pays off for at-risk patients, not healthy low-risk adults.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An illustration shows a human heart with blood vessels over an electrocardiogram waveform. Dr. Vijay D'Silva argues early ECG screening can catch silent heart disease before symptoms appear.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians develop coronary artery disease at younger ages, so the diaspora with family history of early heart disease should raise ECG screening at their annual physical.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Daily Walk Alone Won't Build Fitness: Intensity, Variety, Strength Training Matter
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Fitness expert Sumit Dubey says most walkers stall because comfortable-pace strolls never push the heart and lungs — faster intervals, varied routes, and strength work close the gap.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A group of women power walking outdoors. Fitness expert Sumit Dubey says intensity — walking fast enough to talk but not sing — matters more than duration for cardiovascular fitness.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For NRIs rooted in walking culture, the coach's advice translates to layering intensity bursts and two weekly resistance sessions onto the familiar daily walk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Cardiologist's Three Longevity Habits: Lp(a) Test, Strength Training, Treated Sleep Apnea
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Interventional cardiologist Dr. Sanjay Bhojraj says three underused steps — a one-time Lp(a) blood test, training for functional strength, and treating sleep apnea — can meaningfully slow how fast your heart ages.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A seated cable row exercise. Cardiologist Dr. Sanjay Bhojraj lists strength training among his three longevity habits, alongside an Lp(a) test and treating sleep apnea.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry elevated lipoprotein(a) more often than many populations, making the once-in-a-lifetime Lp(a) test the 2026 ACC/AHA guideline now recommends especially relevant for the Indian diaspora.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Drooping smile, weak arms: neurologists flag stroke warning signs in young adults
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A drooping smile, a weak arm and slurred speech are the classic red flags — and with four in ten Indian stroke patients now under 50, neurologists say young adults should learn the BEFAST checklist and act within the golden hours.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Brain scans. Neurologists warn that a drooping smile, weak arms, and slurred speech can signal a stroke.

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians develop cardiovascular risk factors earlier and at higher rates, making BEFAST stroke awareness especially relevant in NRI households — and for spotting warning signs in ageing parents back home.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Crispy Corn: How to Make the Restaurant-Style Spicy Snack at Home

food.title: Why Modak Became Lord Ganesha's Favourite Sweet, According to Mythology

food.title: Microlot coffee: Inside India's limited-edition world of specialty brews

food.title: MasterChef's Jyoti Vishnani on Building an Indian Kitchen Under ₹10,000

food.title: Which Roti Wins on Protein, Fibre, Iron and Calcium? Nutritionist's Answer

food.nri_angle: Every one of these flours — ragi, jowar, bajra, makki, rajgira — is stocked in Indian grocery stores across the US and Canada, usually at prices close to wheat atta.

travel.title: Twenty-Five Years After 9/11, U.S. Begins Rolling Back Travel Restrictions
travel.excerpt: From the end of the shoes-off rule to water bottles for PreCheck members and gate access at 13 airports, a quarter century after the attacks the U.S. is easing the checkpoint rituals that defined a generation of travel.

travel.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora — heavy long-haul flyers with Diwali travel weeks away — the shoe-rule rollback eases journeys for elderly parents, a water-bottle exception would help families with children, and gateside access restores the ritual of farewell at the gate.

travel.title: Seven Weekend Getaways From Delhi You Can Reach by Bus

travel.title: Kolkata's Floating Hotel Has a Railway Track Running Through It

travel.title: IRCTC Shatters Records as 20 Lakh Tickets Booked in a Single Day
